surfaces.rationale: The published checker interfaces that claimed modules and adopters import: executable contracts and the decision kinds (Regula.Contract), decision registration (Regula.Decision), material claims (Regula.MaterialClaim) and assumptions (Regula.Assumption). Every declaration is checked under its exact transitive axiom set. The registration attributes are elaboration-time code that Lean runs; their effect on a module's .olean is trusted, not proved.

Pure policy categories, structural identities and invariant-preserving collections that the rule registry, the manifest reader and the option allowlist of RG2006 read. Every declaration is checked under its exact transitive axiom set. Their proofs concern the supplied data, not the authenticity of compiler or filesystem observations, compiled machine code, or semantic adequacy.

Cold-start verification driver with exact proof-bearing argument selection, and the module that registers its decisions' kinds; the driver itself imports only the toolchain. Recipes are interpreted through a trusted process IO boundary under verify.sh's single external deadline; the proof does not authenticate subprocess execution.

Toolchain-only dependency provisioning, which acquires no Mathlib by default and, when asked for the Mathlib integration package, provisions one shared, read-only Mathlib per pinned revision and toolchain, and the module that registers its decisions' kinds. The proofs concern the pure decisions it executes: receipt admission is sound, only a link to the shared checkout is kept for Mathlib, removal from a copy is confined to links and clean Git checkouts, only a receipt that names a shared directory identifies it for removal, registering drops no copy, a shared directory is removed only when it is not the current one and no registered copy still links it, and the Mathlib integration check applies exactly to a copy whose integration package selects the repository's toolchain. The packages it pins are those that Lake's load of the integration package materializes: the entry selected for each name is the last of the manifest's entries and then the package overrides file's, and the packages directory is the one the manifest records, a manifest without one being refused (selectPins_sound, mem_gitPins, gitPins_complete, checkoutPin_gitPins). Copies execute the shared construction source, whose observer-model contracts are in RegulaCore.CopyConstruction. The shared-cache link is made in a new directory that mkdir creates. RegulaProvision.Link proves over the filesystem model, for the operations the driver runs, that an entry already at that directory's place makes the link installation fail with nothing changed by it, from the assumption RefusesOccupied that mkdir refuses an existing entry, and that a run which succeeds leaves a link at the path and no entry at that place, from the assumption ReadsEntry that the driver's read of an entry is the model's. RegulaProvision.Ownership proves over the filesystem model, for the read of a real path that the driver runs, that the pins it admits leave out only the path entry for regula whose directory resolves to the real path of the root being provisioned, from the assumption ReadsReal that this read is the model's. Git, Lake and its manifest readers, chmod, ln, mkdir, that read of an entry, rename, rmdir, file locking and Mathlib's cache tool remain trusted process and filesystem effects.

The pure qualification assertions that the site's programs evaluate: evaluate accepts exactly a list whose assertions all hold and otherwise names its first false one. The contract concerns the supplied Lean data, not the authenticity of process, filesystem or compiler observations.

The rule registry and the pure decisions that the checker's programs execute: the rule identities and descriptors, the guidance and setup decisions of the regula command, the site's editions, pages and checks, the Markdown and prose checks, and the shared filesystem constructor, whose contract is over the existing observer model, with checked correspondence to its IO program and explicit native primitive hypotheses. Their contracts concern the supplied data; Lake loading, the compiler and native filesystem effects remain trusted observations.

The complete-application dogfooding surface, imported only from Lean's core libraries and the published checker interfaces: admission, update, and strict state/error composition contracts are proved about the definitions auditApp runs, alongside the retained total fold; its refinement to an abstract capacity model is claimed in the Audit library of the audit/ package. The limiter state/error operations and their proofs are choice-free; the input parser and dependent required-contract interface transitively use Classical.choice through core String internals, as does the IO root. The surface claim is standard-logical and each declaration retains its exact axiom report. The IO shell is trusted execution substrate, so the execution mode stays report.

excluded-libraries.rationale: Regula's checker shell and the repository's own programs, which are not a conforming proof surface yet: the closed input and its loader (Regula.Load, which reads the finished build through Lean's and Lake's interfaces and frees each environment's data with an unsafe call), the rule functions over the input, whose proofs against the specification of the smaller Regula are leaf #487's, the manifest reader, the regula command, the site builder, the local gate, the release checks and the registry checks. Their process, filesystem, Lake and Lean observations are trusted.

excluded-executables.rationale: Rule-reference site builder; its root module belongs to the excluded Regula library. It generates the website from the registry and the rule explanations, renders it with the pinned Verso package and checks the artifact through the claimed RegulaCore.Site decisions; its process, filesystem and Verso observations are not a conforming proof surface.

Lake lint driver, Regula's checker; its root module belongs to the excluded Regula library. It loads the finished build, runs the rule functions over the closed input and prints their findings; its loader and rule functions are not yet proved, which is leaf #487's work.

Project setup (init, doctor) and offline rule guidance (explain, rules, agent-guide, skill); its root module belongs to the excluded Regula library. Its command parser, every text it prints and the setup decision it executes, with their proofs, are the claimed RegulaCore.Guidance, RegulaCore.Feedback and RegulaCore.Setup definitions; the operational Regula.Cli.Setup observes the project through Lake, writes the planned edits and confirms them by observing again. Lake loading, the parsers that locate the edits, and the filesystem are trusted.
